name: Ramp
tagline: Practical, product-ish coding that grows in levels; builders only

values.name: We only hire builders
values.meaning: Solve hard problems, build without permission, ship work you are proud of.

values.name: If it doesn't save you time or money, we don't build it
values.meaning: Judge work by time or money saved for customers.

values.name: 'Hands off' doesn't exist at Ramp
values.meaning: Everyone does hands-on work whatever their role.

values.name: We're a proud meritocracy
values.meaning: Recognition follows the work, not titles.

values.name: Working at Ramp is a bet on yourself
values.meaning: Take big responsibility and grow fast.

loop.focus: One multi-level practical problem, about 90 min (uncertain).
Pair-programming on practical build tasks, not classic LeetCode (uncertain).
Technical plus a values-based behavioral talk (uncertain).

behavioral_themes: Something you built without being asked
coding_style: Practical, product-like tasks such as an in-memory system, CRUD over records, or calling an API, with requirements added in stages (uncertain). Graded on clean, working code that adapts as requirements change, plus thinking out loud with the interviewer.
rubric: Code that refactors cleanly as requirements grow
question_themes: In-memory store or bank API with staged features
CRUD over a list of records
DFS over data fetched from an API
Add a feature to make a failing test pass

panel_flavor.manager: Maya asks what you built on your own initiative and how much time or money it saved real users.
panel_flavor.tech: Theo pairs on a product-like task, then adds a new requirement each level to see if your code bends or breaks.
panel_flavor.skeptic: Sol asks whether you would join this candidate if they started a company, and wants shipped proof and numbers, not plans.

uncertain: No official Ramp page describes the interview; loop details come from candidate reports
Intern loop length and whether system design appears for interns
'Slope' as an interview term comes from a third-party guide
Values above are principles stated on the careers page, not a formal values list
